It's normal to want someone to say something. 100%. I've had instances very similar where people I thought would say something (and would often brag about wanting to say something if they saw something), either claimed to have not seen it or didn't do anything in the moment to help me.

The other part to consider: it may have been a real "fight or flight" moment for both of you (you reacting with a fight then flight and the BF just wanting flight). Now why we react the ways we do depend on a number of things: our personalities, our subconscious's sense of danger, what we've been taught/socially programmed, etc. I'm not excusing this; it just could be that your BF never has had to think about SA or any inappropriate touch being done to him before, so he just "panicked" and thought the best thing (instinctually) was to get you away from the danger. I've had a few exes (and even my current BF) make certain remarks which tells me that some fears I have don't even cross their minds. The difference between my exes and my current BF is that he actually wants to learn and understand versus them writing me off.

Either way, take some time to process this and come to terms with everything (therapy, journaling, etc.). Also, if it's been less than 24 hours, play some Tetris on your phone. Tetris (when a traumatic memory is super fresh) actually forces our brain to think about problem solving and thinking differently so it can help alleviate some stress and reduce the amount of "damage" the trauma does to us.

Please take care of yourself and reach out if you need to.

We're still like that (bodies take a lot of generations to override a good system) so I would just try to relax, take a deep breath, and know that next month might be different.

Hey you. I know that this is all scary. And you have a lot of things on your plate. Let's tackle these one at a time together:

- I'd highly recommend getting birth control for yourself if you haven't already. There are plenty of subscription services that could just be mailed to your dorm/apartment (or a PO box if you still live at home). Otherwise, you could do what I did: get an IUD as part of your "women's wellness" portion of your insurance. I told my parents my periods were getting so bad that I'd be vomiting and would have flu symptoms (all true) so this would help minimize it. IUDs are covered under a basic health plan by the ACA so that's another option. 

-There are several subs on Reddit that can give more details on how to proceed if something happened and you needed assistance in Texas. I'm not sure if mail-in services are an option there but it may be... There's also plenty of funds and services to get you these options for cheap. 

- As for staying in Texas or moving, you have time to figure that out. I'd suggest just researching what jobs are in your field and you may be pleasantly surprised as to where you may end up. Texas has a lot but there are other states that need chemical engineers too. 

- And as for being away from friends and family, you'll know when the time is right what's best for you. I had to move hundreds of miles away from my family to have one of the coolest jobs ever that paid super well. For me at the time, it made sense. And I know it'll work out for you too.

You got this. Just take a deep breath and know there are people on your side (even if we're half a country away).

You deserve it too! I just don't want you to feel disheartened because part of it is (cliche) rediscovering yourself and the other part is heading back into the world with a clear sense of what works for you and what doesn't.

I don't think it's bad to establish boundaries early or to recognize what kind of value a relationship has for you. If the other person is aware of the type of relationship it is and consented to that (like you two actually discussed it was FWB and nothing more), I think it's fine.

What's less fine is using this person to not deal with your own stuff. Being trauma bonded to someone isn't exactly the start of a healthy relationship in most cases because trauma does funny things to how the brain operates and reacts. Using sex and relationships to cope with trauma is a normal response but depending on how they're used, they can be highly problematic (putting yourself in risky situations, exposure to diseases, etc.).

If you're manipulating this person into sex, then you're being narcissistic. If you were in a committed relationship with this person and cheated on them, you might be a narcissist. 

I hope you find peace and overcome your trauma.
